stem: Which of the following equations has exactly one real solution?
solution: A quadratic has exactly one real solution when its discriminant \(b^{2} - 4ac\) is \(0\), that is, when it is a perfect square.
\(x^{2} - 8x + 16 = (x - 4)^{2}\), which is \(0\) only when \(x = 4\). The other equations have two real solutions (\(\pm 4\); \(3\) and \(5\)) or none (\(x^{2} = -16\)).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(x^{2} = 16\) has two real solutions, \(4\) and \(-4\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(x^{2} = -16\) has no real solutions, since a square is never negative.
explanation.D: Incorrect. \((x - 3)(x - 5) = 0\) has two real solutions, \(3\) and \(5\).
